stem: The scientific notation of 0.00002019 is
reasons: Moving the decimal five places to the right gives 2.019, so the exponent is −5.
This would give 0.0002019, ten times the stated number.
A positive exponent makes the answer much larger than 1.
A positive exponent of five gives 201,900.

stem: Which of the following instruments is used to measure the internal diameter of a pipe?
reasons: A metre rule does not reach the internal diameter accurately.
A standard screw gauge measures small external dimensions.
The internal jaws of Vernier callipers contact opposite sides of the pipe’s bore.
A measuring cylinder measures volume.

stem: An athlete runs around a circular track of radius 50 m and finishes at the same point where he began his journey. His total displacement in metre(s) is evaluated to be
reasons: Displacement is final position minus initial position. The runner finishes at the start, so the displacement is 0 m.
The runner returns to the same position, so there is no nonzero displacement.
The circumference gives the distance travelled, while the displacement is zero.
100π m is the distance of one lap, not the displacement.

stem: A distance-time graph of a moving object is given below. With reference to the given graph, the distance covered during 10 to 12 hours is
reasons: The line is flat at 10 km from hour 10 to hour 12, so no additional distance is covered.
The interval is 2 hours. Its distance change is 0 km.
A distance of 5 km would require a rise of 5 km on the vertical axis.
10 km is the cumulative reading throughout the interval, not the increase.

stem: A car starts from rest and has uniform acceleration of 10 m/s². After some time it possess the velocity of 30 m/s. The distance covered by the car during this time is
reasons: 920 m does not follow from v² = u² + 2as.
Use the square of 30 m/s together with 2 × 10 m/s², which gives 45 m.
Substitution into s = (v² − u²)/(2a) gives 45 m.
From rest, s = 30²/(2 × 10) = 45 m.

stem: A boy starts his travelling from a point P and ends at point S. The magnitude of displacement from point P to S is
reasons: The two horizontal 5 m segments cancel. The final position is 3 m directly above the starting point.
5 m is the length of each horizontal leg, and the legs cancel.
8 m counts part of the path. Displacement uses only the start and end positions.
13 m is the total path length 5 + 3 + 5, not the displacement.

stem: The momentum of a moving truck as shown in the given diagram is
reasons: This comes from subtracting the speed from the mass, which mixes units.
This comes from adding the numerical values of mass and speed, which mixes units.
Momentum equals mass multiplied by velocity: 4,000 × 22 = 88,000 kg·m/s in the direction shown.
Momentum is linear in speed. It is not calculated by squaring the speed.

stem: In the given figure, two blocks of masses m₁ and m₂ are attached with an inextensible string such that the pulley and the horizontal surface are frictionless. If the blocks are at rest, then the tension in the string at point A will be
options: equal to tension at point B.
less than tension at point B.
greater than tension at point B.
reasons: An ideal string under load carries a nonzero tension.
For an ideal massless string over a frictionless pulley, the tension at A equals the tension at B.
The frictionless pulley changes the direction of the force without reducing its magnitude.
The ideal pulley does not increase tension on either side.
reviewNote: The statement that the blocks stay at rest requires a restraint or another balancing force. Equality of the two tensions follows from the ideal string and pulley, even if the blocks accelerate.

stem: An object is moving on a horizontal surface. The force exerted by the horizontal surface that opposes the motion of the object is
reasons: Weight acts downward and is not the horizontal force from the surface.
Gravity is not the contact force exerted by the surface.
Tension is a pull in a string or similar object.
Sliding friction acts along the surface opposite the relative motion.

stem: In an elastic collision, which of the following also remains conserved along with momentum?
reasons: Potential energy can change temporarily during compression, but kinetic energy before and after is the defining comparison.
An elastic collision conserves total kinetic energy as well as total momentum.
Sound is one way mechanical energy can be transferred out of the motion, not the defining conserved quantity.
Thermal energy is not the additional conserved mechanical quantity used to identify an elastic collision.

stem: If the maximum moment of force on a door is 10 N·m by an applied force of 2.25 N, then the distance of handle from hinge (pivot) is
reasons: Use the moment divided by the force, with the force perpendicular at maximum moment.
At maximum moment the applied force is perpendicular to the lever arm, so r = 10/2.25 ≈ 4.444 m.
Adding a torque to a force mixes units.
22.5 is the product 10 × 2.25. The lever arm requires division.

stem: Two forces act at the right angle at point O, as shown in the given figure. What will be the magnitude and direction of the resultant force?
reasons: The forces are perpendicular. Their resultant has magnitude √(12² + 9²) = 15 N and points along OQ, the diagonal from O.
15 N is the right magnitude, but PR points along the other diagonal.
OQ is the correct direction, but 21 N adds the perpendicular magnitudes directly.
Neither direct addition nor the other diagonal gives the resultant.

stem: Let suppose, a hole is drilled through the Earth along the diameter and a stone is dropped into it. When the stone reaches the centre of the Earth keeping same size and shape, it has constant
reasons: The stone’s mass is unchanged as it moves through the Earth.
Weight depends on the local gravitational field and is zero at the centre in the symmetric model.
Momentum depends on velocity, which changes as the stone falls.
The acceleration varies with position inside Earth and is zero at the centre in the symmetric model.

stem: A satellite is revolving around the Earth in a circular orbit with a velocity v. If the gravitational force between the satellite and the Earth suddenly disappears, then the velocity of the satellite will be
reasons: The satellite retains its instantaneous velocity immediately after the force disappears.
With no net force, it continues at the same speed v along the tangent at the point where gravity vanishes.
There is no impulse to double the speed.
Removing the inward force does not increase the speed.

stem: If the radius of the Earth shrinks by 1%, while its mass remains the same, then the acceleration due to gravity on the Earth’s surface would
reasons: For fixed Earth mass, g = GM/r². Reducing r increases g.
The inverse-square relation gives an increase as the radius decreases.
A fixed mass does not keep g fixed when the radius changes.
The inverse-square relation predicts the direction of change.

stem: If a planet comes closer to the Sun, then the planet will
options: keep moving with the same speed as earlier.
reasons: A planet moves faster on the closer part of a bound orbit. A smaller circular orbit about the same Sun also has greater orbital speed.
In the intended orbital comparison, the nearer motion is faster.
Moving closer on a bound orbit does not by itself make the planet collide with the Sun.
Orbital speed depends on distance from the Sun in the comparisons assumed here.
reviewNote: The answer assumes the planet moves closer on the same bound orbit, or compares circular orbits around the same Sun. The stem does not specify what caused the change.

stem: An astronaut returns from the Moon to the Earth. Which of the following is the CORRECT description about his/ her mass and weight?
options: Less on Earth than Moon · Same on Earth and Moon
More on Earth than Moon · Same on Earth and Moon
Same on Earth and Moon · Less on Earth than Moon
Same on Earth and Moon · More on Earth than Moon
reasons: The astronaut’s mass does not change and Earth’s stronger gravity increases weight.
Mass stays the same while weight increases on Earth.
The weight is greater on Earth because local gravity is stronger.
The same mass experiences greater weight on Earth because g is larger there.

stem: A car travels a distance of 150 m in the direction of a constant force of 50 N. The work done on the car is
reasons: Work in the force direction is the product Fd.
Adding, subtracting or dividing the given force and distance does not compute work.
Work is 50 × 150 joules.
The force and displacement are aligned, so W = Fd = 50 × 150 = 7,500 J.

stem: A car has stopped after screeching to avoid a crash with a van. With reference to the given situation, the kinetic energy of the car will then be converted into
reasons: The screech carries some energy as sound, and friction produces heat.
Braking friction converts most of the lost kinetic energy into thermal energy and some into sound.
The scenario gives a sound and provides no reason to assume increased potential energy.
The braking dissipates energy as heat, which this option omits.

stem: If a loading truck has an output of 3600 J and its efficiency is 50%, then the input provided to the truck will be
reasons: The input must exceed the useful output because the efficiency is below 100%.
This is below the stated output and inconsistent with 50% efficiency.
Efficiency = output/input = 0.50, so input = 3,600/0.50 = 7,200 J.
At 50% efficiency the input is twice, not three times, the output.

stem: As compared to the sea level, atmospheric pressure on mountains
reasons: A mountain has a shorter column of atmosphere above it, so the air pressure is lower.
A higher pressure generally occurs lower in the atmosphere.
Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude.
Weather can affect a reading, but the general decrease with altitude is predictable.

stem: While drinking juice with the help of a straw from a juice can, the air pressure inside the straw will
reasons: Raising the internal pressure would oppose the upward push from outside.
Reducing the pressure in the straw lets the atmospheric pressure on the liquid surface push the juice upward.
The liquid rises because a pressure difference is created.
Suction lowers the pressure in the straw relative to the surroundings.

stem: A change caused by stress in original shape, volume or length is called as
reasons: Strain measures the deformation caused by stress, usually as a change relative to the original dimension.
Density is mass per unit volume.
Pressure is normal force per unit area.
Elasticity is the ability to recover shape after the deforming force is removed.

stem: If the temperature of a gas is increased continuously, then which of the following energies increases in the gas molecules?
reasons: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. The molecular quantity tied to the gas temperature is average kinetic energy.
Warming an ordinary gas does not imply an increase in light energy in its molecules.
The average translational kinetic energy of gas molecules increases as the absolute temperature rises.
In the ideal-gas model the temperature relation is with molecular kinetic energy, not intermolecular potential energy.

stem: If the temperature of a hot pot is 125°C, then its temperature in kelvin will be
reasons: Add 273.15 to the Celsius reading rather than subtracting the Celsius value from 273.
There is no conversion rule that gives 225 K here.
125°C equals 398.15 K, not 257 K.
T = 125 + 273.15 = 398.15 K, or 398 K to the nearest kelvin.

stem: When Sun rays fall on a stone and water in a beaker, the stone becomes hot quickly as compared to water. This is because the stone has
options: less latent heat of fusion than water.
less specific heat capacity than water.
reasons: For equal mass and absorbed energy, a higher heat capacity gives a smaller temperature rise.
Expansion changes dimensions, not how much energy is needed per degree in this comparison.
Latent heat of fusion concerns melting. Neither sample has to melt here.
For equal mass and absorbed heat, ΔT = Q/(mc). A smaller specific heat capacity gives the stone a larger temperature rise.
reviewNote: The intended comparison assumes comparable mass and energy absorbed. In real sunlight, surface absorptivity, container and sample mass can also affect the heating rate.

stem: In evaporation, water starts converting into vapours
reasons: Evaporation is not restricted to 4°C.
Water molecules can escape from a liquid surface at any temperature at which liquid water is present.
Liquid water evaporates below the boiling point.
Evaporation occurs over a much wider temperature range than 0–4°C.

stem: If the thickness of a wall is doubled, then the thermal conductivity will
reasons: Doubling thickness can halve the heat-transfer rate under fixed conditions. The material’s conductivity stays constant.
Thermal resistance doubles under fixed conditions, while thermal conductivity is unchanged.
There is no inverse-square dependence on thickness for steady conduction through a flat wall.
Thermal conductivity is a material property. Doubling the thickness changes the thermal resistance, while the conductivity stays the same.
reviewNote: The published key displays an asterisk and does not specify an answer letter. Practice scores D because thermal conductivity is a material property.

stem:
Heat reaches the surface of the Earth from the Sun MAINLY because of

I. Radiation

II. Convection

III. Conduction
reasons: Radiation carries solar energy across the near-vacuum of space to Earth.
Conduction needs matter to transfer thermal energy across a region.
Convection can redistribute energy after sunlight arrives, but it cannot carry it across space.
Convection and conduction require a material medium, so neither is the mechanism across space.

stem: All of the following factors affect the rate of transfer of energy in radiation EXCEPT
options: colour and texture of the surface.
reasons: A larger emitting surface sends out more energy at the same temperature and emissivity.
Thermal emission increases as surface temperature rises.
For the board’s simplified isolated-surface comparison, area, temperature and emissivity determine the emitted power. Shape alone is not a separate factor.
Colour and finish can affect how strongly a surface emits infrared radiation.
reviewNote: The board’s answer assumes a simple isolated surface. Geometry can affect the net exchange of radiation between surfaces that face or partly shield one another.
